results.label: Definition 1.1 (Deterministic exact-real query model).
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem1] Definition 1.1 (Deterministic exact-real query model).
 [S1.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
The method knows  $x_{0},L,R,p,\kappa$  and, in the target-accuracy version,  $\varepsilon$ . After any finite exact transcript, its next query, stopping decision, and output are deterministic single-valued functions of that transcript and the known parameters. Each oracle invocation, including a repeated query, counts once; the output need not be a previously queried point. Exact-real operations involving only the known parameters and the transcript are uncharged. We make no finite-precision, arithmetic, or bit-complexity claim.

results.label: Theorem 1.2 (Exact-real gradient-query upper bound).
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem2] Theorem 1.2 (Exact-real gradient-query upper bound).
 [S1.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
Let  $d\geq 1$ ,  $2\leq p<\infty$ ,  $1<\kappa\leq 2$ ,  $q=p/(p-1)$ ,  $L,R\geq 0$ ,  $\varepsilon>0$ , and  $x_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . Let  $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$  be convex and differentiable, satisfy (1.1), and have a minimizer satisfying (1.2). In the model of Definition 1.1, the accumulative shifted-power regularization method in Section 3 returns  $x$  with  $\left\lVert\nabla f(x)\right\rVert_{q}\leq\varepsilon$  after at most
 [S1.E5] 
 $C_{p,\kappa}\!\left[1+\left(\frac{LR^{\kappa-1}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\beta}\right]\quad\text{gradient queries},\qquad\beta=\frac{p}{\kappa p+\kappa-p}.$ (1.5)

Here  $C_{p,\kappa}<\infty$  is independent of  $d,L,R,\varepsilon$ . If  $\varepsilon\geq LR^{\kappa-1}$ , the method returns  $x_{0}$  without a query. In the nontrivial regime  $0<\varepsilon<LR^{\kappa-1}$ , the additive  $1$  can be absorbed into  $C_{p,\kappa}(LR^{\kappa-1}/\varepsilon)^{\beta}$ .

results.label: Corollary 1.3 (Conditional minimax comparison).
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem3] Corollary 1.3 (Conditional minimax comparison).
 [S1.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
Assume the simultaneous normalized hard-family realization in assumption 6.1. Fix  $2\leq p<\infty$ ,  $1<\kappa\leq 2$ , and  $L,R>0$ . There are  $c_{p,\kappa},C_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{lb}}>0$ , depending only on  $p,\kappa$ . For  $\beta=p/(\kappa p+\kappa-p)$ , every integer  $d\geq 1$  and  $\varepsilon>0$  with  $0<\varepsilon\leq c_{p,\kappa}LR^{\kappa-1}$ ,  $\log d\geq p$ , and
 [S1.Ex1] 
 $d\geq C_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{lb}}\left(\frac{LR^{\kappa-1}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\beta}$ 

obey the matching relation
 [S1.Ex2] 
 $\operatorname{Comp}^{\mathrm{det}}_{p,d,\kappa}(L,R,\varepsilon)=\Theta_{p,\kappa}\!\left(\left(\frac{LR^{\kappa-1}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\beta}\right).$ 

The upper-bound half is unconditional.

results.label: Corollary 1.4 (Schatten- $p$  upper bound).
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem4] Corollary 1.4 (Schatten- $p$  upper bound).
 [S1.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
Let  $m,n\geq 1$ ,  $k=\min\{m,n\}$ ,  $2\leq p<\infty$ ,  $1<\kappa\leq 2$ ,  $q=p/(p-1)$ ,  $L,R\geq 0$ , and  $\varepsilon>0$ . Fix  $X_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ . On  $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ , define
 [S1.Ex3] 
 $\left\lVert X\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{p}}=\left(\sum_{j=1}^{k}\sigma_{j}(X)^{p}\right)^{1/p}$ 

and take gradients with respect to the trace pairing. Suppose that a convex differentiable  $f:\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\to\mathbb{R}$  satisfies
 [S1.Ex4] 
 $\left\lVert\nabla f(X)-\nabla f(Y)\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{q}}\leq L\left\lVert X-Y\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{p}}^{\kappa-1}$ 

and has a minimizer  $X^{*}$  with  $\left\lVert X_{0}-X^{*}\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{p}}\leq R$ . In the matrix analogue of Definition 1.1, with  $X_{0},L,R,p,\kappa,\varepsilon$  known, there is a gradient-query method returning  $X$  with  $\left\lVert\nabla f(X)\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{q}}\leq\varepsilon$  within the bound (1.5), independently of  $m,n$ . For  $p>2$ , this statement treats the nonseparable multicenter prox as an exact uncharged map and makes no finite-precision, arithmetic, or bit-complexity claim.

results.label: Lemma 2.1 (Normalized shifted-power atom).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 2.1 (Normalized shifted-power atom).
 [S2.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Let  $d\geq 1$ ,  $2\leq p<\infty$ ,  $q=p/(p-1)$ , and  $c\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . Define
 [S2.E4] 
 $a_{p}=2^{p-2},\qquad\omega_{c}(x)=\frac{a_{p}}{p}\left\lVert x-c\right\rVert_{p}^{p}.$ (2.4)

Then  $\omega_{c}$  is  $(1,p)$ -uniformly convex in the convention (2.1), and
 [S2.E5] 
 $\nabla\omega_{c}(x)=a_{p}J_{p}(x-c),\qquad\left\lVert J_{p}(v)\right\rVert_{q}=\left\lVert v\right\rVert_{p}^{p-1}.$ (2.5)

Consequently, every finite sum  $\sum_{i=1}^{m}b_{i}\omega_{c_{i}}$  with  $b_{i}>0$  is  $(\sum_{i=1}^{m}b_{i},p)$ -uniformly convex.

results.label: Lemma 2.2 (Complementary-composite contraction).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 2.2 (Complementary-composite contraction).
 [S2.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
Let  $d\geq 1$ ,  $L>0$ ,  $2\leq p<\infty$ ,  $1<\kappa\leq 2$ ,  $q=p/(p-1)$ , and  $c\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . Let  $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$  be convex and differentiable and satisfy (1.1). Let  $H$  be a known  $(\mu,p)$ -uniformly convex function with  $\mu>0$ . Suppose that, for every  $g\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$  and  $A,m>0$ , the internal minimization of  $\left\langle g,x\right\rangle+AH(x)+m\omega_{c}(x)$  is available. Let  $z^{*}$  minimize  $F=f+H$ , and suppose  $\left\lVert c-z^{*}\right\rVert_{p}\leq D$  for  $D>0$ . Put
 [S2.E6] 
 $\Delta=\kappa p+\kappa-p,\qquad\beta=\frac{p}{\Delta}.$ (2.6)

For  $0<\delta\leq D$ , Generalized AGD+ with its coefficients and budget fixed from these parameters returns a transcript-dependent point  $z$  with  $\left\lVert z-z^{*}\right\rVert_{p}\leq\delta$  using at most
 [S2.E7] 
 $C_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{cc}}\!\left[1+\left(\frac{L}{\mu\delta^{p-\kappa}}\right)^{\beta}\left(\frac{D}{\delta}\right)^{\kappa\beta}\right]$ (2.7)

gradient queries to  $f$ . The same fixed budget guarantees
 [S2.E8] 
 $F(z)-F(z^{*})\leq\frac{\mu}{p}\delta^{p}.$ (2.8)

results.label: Lemma 4.1 (Minimizer transport and stage contraction).
results.statement:
[S4.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 4.1 (Minimizer transport and stage contraction).
 [S4.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For every  $s=1,\ldots,S$ ,
 [S4.E1] 
 $\left\lVert x_{s}^{*}-x_{s-1}\right\rVert_{p}\leq\delta_{s-1},\qquad\left\lVert x_{s}-x_{s}^{*}\right\rVert_{p}\leq\delta_{s}.$ (4.1)

results.label: Lemma 4.2 (Path bound).
results.statement:
[S4.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 4.2 (Path bound).
 [S4.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
For every  $1\leq i\leq S$ ,
 [S4.E2] 
 $\left\lVert x_{S}^{*}-x_{i-1}\right\rVert_{p}\leq U\delta_{i-1},\qquad U=\frac{\rho+1}{\rho-1}=3.$ (4.2)

results.label: Remark 5.1 (Why the dual norm is the dimension-free target).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem1] Remark 5.1 (Why the dual norm is the dimension-free target).
 [S5.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For  $q\leq s<\infty$ , norm monotonicity gives  $\left\lVert g\right\rVert_{s}\leq\left\lVert g\right\rVert_{q}$ , so Theorem 1.2 also certifies every such weaker  $\ell_{s}$  target. No dimension-free conversion is possible in the opposite direction: if  $1\leq s<q$  and  $g=d^{-1/q}(1,\ldots,1)$ , then
 [S5.Ex4] 
 $\left\lVert g\right\rVert_{q}=1,\qquad\left\lVert g\right\rVert_{s}=d^{1/s-1/q}.$ 

Thus a stronger  $\ell_{s}$  target is a different oracle problem.

results.label: Corollary 5.2 (Accuracy-oblivious checkpoints).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem2] Corollary 5.2 (Accuracy-oblivious checkpoints).
 [S5.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.2, except for a prescribed target  $\varepsilon$ , there is a deterministic procedure producing checkpoints  $z_{1},z_{2},\ldots$ . If  $Q_{j}$  denotes the total number of gradient queries through checkpoint  $j$ , then
 [S5.Ex5] 
 $\left\lVert\nabla f(z_{j})\right\rVert_{q}\leq LR^{\kappa-1}2^{-j},\qquad Q_{j}\leq C_{p,\kappa}2^{j\beta},$ 

where  $\beta=p/(\kappa p+\kappa-p)$ . Hence prior knowledge of  $\varepsilon$  is unnecessary, with no multiplicative logarithmic loss in the final query rate; the wrapper still uses  $L,R,p,\kappa$ .

results.label: Remark 5.3 (Other Schatten gradient targets).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem3] Remark 5.3 (Other Schatten gradient targets).
 [S5.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
Let  $k=\min\{m,n\}$ . If  $q\leq s<\infty$ , then  $\left\lVert G\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{s}}\leq\left\lVert G\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{q}}$ , so Corollary 1.4 certifies the  $\mathsf{S}_{s}$  target without any change. If  $1\leq s<q$ , the sharp norm conversion is
 [S5.Ex18] 
 $\left\lVert G\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{s}}\leq k^{1/s-1/q}\left\lVert G\right\rVert_{\mathsf{S}_{q}}.$ 

Running the corollary with dual-norm tolerance  $\varepsilon k^{-(1/s-1/q)}$  therefore gives the valid bound
 [S5.Ex19] 
 $O_{p,\kappa}\!\left[1+\left(\frac{LR^{\kappa-1}k^{1/s-1/q}}{\varepsilon}\right)^{p/(\kappa p+\kappa-p)}\right].$ 

The dimensional norm factor cannot be improved. Equality is attained by
 [S5.Ex20] 
 $G=k^{-1/q}\operatorname{Diag}_{m,n}(1,\ldots,1).$ 

This is a sharpness statement for norm conversion, not a matching oracle lower bound for the stronger  $\mathsf{S}_{s}$  target.

results.label: Assumption 6.1 (Simultaneous normalized hard-family interface).
results.statement:
[S6.Thmtheorem1] Assumption 6.1 (Simultaneous normalized hard-family interface).
 [S6.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Fix  $2\leq p<\infty$ ,  $1<\kappa\leq 2$ , and put  $q=p/(p-1)$  and  $\beta=p/(\kappa p+\kappa-p)$ . There are positive constants  $c_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{obj}},C_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{obj}},c_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{qry}}$ , depending only on  $p,\kappa$ , with the following property. If an integer  $d\geq 1$  and  $\zeta$  satisfy
 [S6.Ex1] 
 $0<\zeta\leq c_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{obj}},\qquad\log d\geq p,\qquad d\geq C_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{obj}}\zeta^{-\beta},$ 

then, for every deterministic local-oracle method starting from the origin, there is a normalized unconstrained  $\ell_{p}^{d}$  instance  $F$  such that no queried point has objective gap at most  $\zeta$  before  $c_{p,\kappa}^{\mathrm{qry}}\zeta^{-\beta}$  calls. The instance satisfies
 [S6.Ex2] 
 $\left\lVert\nabla F(x)-\nabla F(y)\right\rVert_{q}\leq\left\lVert x-y\right\rVert_{p}^{\kappa-1}.$ 

Moreover, the same instance is realized as  $F=\mathcal{S}h/\mu$  for an integer  $M\geq 1$ , parameters  $\bar{\delta},\mu>0$  and  $\eta,r_{\mathrm{h}}\geq 0$ , and vectors  $z_{1},\ldots,z_{M}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$  satisfying  $\left\lVert z_{i}\right\rVert_{q}\leq 1$ .

 [S6.Thmtheorem1.p2] 
All hypotheses of Lemma 6.2 hold:  $h$  has the form (6.3);  $\mathcal{S}$  is convexity-preserving and  $r_{\mathrm{h}}$ -local;  $\mathcal{S}h$  is differentiable; and  $\left\lVert\mathcal{S}h-h\right\rVert_{\infty}\leq\eta$ . These parameters satisfy
 [S6.E2] 
 $r_{\mathrm{h}}\leq\frac{\bar{\delta}}{8},\qquad M\bar{\delta}\leq\mu\zeta,\qquad\eta\leq\frac{\mu\zeta}{4},\qquad 4\mu\zeta\leq 1.$ (6.2)

The queried-point convention above is the one used in the reduction; an arbitrary transcript-measurable output is handled by one appended query.

results.label: Lemma 6.2 (Localization in the hard family).
results.statement:
[S6.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 6.2 (Localization in the hard family).
 [S6.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
Adopt the hard-family notation of Diakonikolas and Guzmán [5, Eq. (3)]. In particular, let  $d,M\geq 1$  be integers,  $2\leq p<\infty$ ,  $q=p/(p-1)$ ,  $\bar{\delta},\mu>0$ ,  $\eta,r_{\mathrm{h}}\geq 0$ , and  $z_{1},\ldots,z_{M}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$  with  $\left\lVert z_{i}\right\rVert_{q}\leq 1$ . Let
 [S6.E3] 
 $h(x)=\max\left\{\frac{1}{2}\max_{1\leq i\leq M}\big(\left\langle z_{i},x\right\rangle-i\bar{\delta}\big),\ \left\lVert x\right\rVert_{p}-C\right\},\qquad C=\frac{1}{2}\bigl(3(1+r_{\mathrm{h}})+M\bar{\delta}\bigr),$ (6.3)

where  $r_{\mathrm{h}}$  is the locality radius. Let  $\mathcal{S}$  be the convexity-preserving local smoothing used in that construction, assume that  $\mathcal{S}h$  is differentiable and  $\left\lVert\mathcal{S}h-h\right\rVert_{\infty}\leq\eta$ , and set  $F=\mathcal{S}h/\mu$ . Then, at every point  $x$  where  $F$  is differentiable,
 [S6.E4] 
 $\bigl(1-\mu\left\lVert\nabla F(x)\right\rVert_{q}\bigr)\left\lVert x\right\rVert_{p}\leq C-\frac{\bar{\delta}}{2}+2\eta.$ (6.4)

results.label: Proposition 7.1 (A supplied diagonal metric for quadratics).
results.statement:
[S7.Thmtheorem1] Proposition 7.1 (A supplied diagonal metric for quadratics).
 [S7.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Let  $d,N\geq 1$ ,  $2\leq p<\infty$ ,  $q=p/(p-1)$ ,  $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ ,  $b,x_{0}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ , and  $R\geq 0$ , where  $d$  and  $N$  are integers. Suppose  $A\succeq 0$ . Define
 [S7.Ex4] 
 $f(x)=\frac{1}{2}x^{\top}Ax-b^{\top}x,\qquad L_{A}=\left\lVert A\right\rVert_{p\to q}:=\sup_{\left\lVert v\right\rVert_{p}\leq 1}\left\lVert Av\right\rVert_{q}.$ 

Suppose that  $f$  has a minimizer  $x^{*}$  with  $\left\lVert x_{0}-x^{*}\right\rVert_{p}\leq R$ . Put
 [S7.Ex5] 
 $s_{2}=\infty,\qquad s_{p}=\frac{p}{p-2}\quad(p>2),\qquad\gamma_{p}=\bigl(\mathbb{E}\left\lvert G\right\rvert^{p}\bigr)^{2/p},\quad G\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1).$ 

We use the endpoint conventions  $1/s_{2}=0$  and  $d^{-1/s_{2}}=1$ . If  $L_{A}=0$ , then  $\nabla f\equiv 0$ . If  $L_{A}>0$ , there exists a positive diagonal matrix  $D=\operatorname{Diag}(w)\succ 0$  such that
 [S7.E10] 
 $D\succeq A,\qquad\left\lVert w\right\rVert_{s_{p}}\leq 2\gamma_{p}L_{A}.$ (7.10)

If  $L_{A}>0$  and this metric is supplied to the algorithm, Hilbert-space mirror-dual concatenation has, after at most  $N$  queries, an output  $x_{N}^{D}$  satisfying
 [S7.E11] 
 $\left\lVert\nabla f(x_{N}^{D})\right\rVert_{q}=O_{p}\!\left(\frac{L_{A}R}{N^{2}}\right).$ (7.11)

For  $L_{A}=0$ , the gradient vanishes identically, so the same estimate holds with output  $x_{0}$  and no queries.
